the nutritional regulation of milk fat and the potential for enhancing the nutritional composition of milk for human health.
the effects of dietary fatty acid composition on the production and composition of milk fat and milk protein in dairy cows.
the development of nutritional strategies for altering the fatty acid composition of milk fat.

the nutritional value of dairy products can be improved by modifying milk fat composition.

nutrition plays an extremely important role in the modification of the milk fatty acid profile and that the use of nutrition as an alternative to genetic selection is an attractive option for the development of milk with enhanced nutritional value.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

milk fatty acid composition can be modified by nutrition, but that the extent of change is limited by the extent to which the rumen microbiota can metabolise fatty acids and the extent to which fatty acids can be absorbed from the rumen and delivered to the mammary gland in a biologically available form.
nutrition is the major environmental regulator of milk fatty acid content and the potential exists for enhancing the nutritional and health benefits of milk fat.
nutrition can be used as an effective tool to alter milk fatty acid composition to enhance the nutritional value of dairy foods.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nutritional strategies that are most successful in enhancing the health value of milk fatty acids are also likely to be the most sustainable in terms of animal welfare and environmental impact.
milk fatty acids, particularly those that are bioactive in nature, are not only a product of genetics but are also highly influenced by diet.
nutrition is an important tool to modify milk fatty acid composition and that this is a sustainable and welfare acceptable strategy for enhancing the nutritional quality of milk and dairy products.
